brief: S&P has been range-bound for three months, with 60-day realized volatility near 10%, bottom-quartile for the COVID/post-COVID era. That calm headline masks stress beneath: the hedge fund VIP pair trade was hit again this week despite a 47bp S&P move, because a terrific first half, including an epic Q2, gave way to a drawdown since late June as crowded AI-theme length unwound. GS's prime brokerage saw sustained net and gross de-risking, with Thursday the heaviest day of tech selling in two years. Fundamentally, AI skepticism has grown even as mega-cap execution and demand hold up, because power and capital constraints are adding uncertainty to the AI buildout's path and sequence. Oil breaking out added another blow, and midterms are an increasingly negative talking point. Pasquariello has limited conviction, but reads de-grossing (vol firming, cyclicals-vs-defensives hit, Risk Appetite Indicator negative for the first time since March) as wall-of-worry support for the bull case. Hyperscaler earnings next week test GS's EPS growth path (+29% 2026, +18% 2027, +11% 2028). Corporate credit has turned ugly beyond AI names, and contacts call conditions melting down.
